passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of a novel weight‑loss supplement on adults aged 25–55 years. Participants were randomly assigned to one of five groups: a control group receiving no supplement, a low‑dose group (10 mg/day), a medium‑dose group (20 mg/day), a high‑dose group (40 mg/day), and a placebo group receiving an inert capsule identical in appearance to the supplement. Over 12 weeks, participants recorded their daily caloric intake and engaged in a standardized 30‑minute aerobic exercise routine three times per week. Body weight was measured at baseline and at the end of the study. The study aimed to determine whether the supplement produced a dose‑dependent reduction in body weight while controlling for dietary and exercise variables.
stem: Which group achieved the greatest mean weight loss according to Table 1?
explanation: The high‑dose group had a mean weight loss of 3.4 kg, the largest value among all groups.
trap: Choosing the placebo group because it sounds active; the greatest mean weight loss is the high-dose group's 3.4 kg.

stem: What type of study design was used in this research?
explanation: Participants were randomly assigned to treatment groups and followed over time, which is the hallmark of a randomized controlled trial.
trap: Choosing an observational cohort design because participants were followed for 12 weeks; random assignment to doses defines an RCT.

stem: Calculate the mean difference in weight loss between the high‑dose group and the control group.
explanation: Mean difference = 3.4 kg (high dose) – 0.5 kg (control) = 2.9 kg.
trap: Reporting the high-dose loss alone (3.4 kg) instead of subtracting the control group's 0.5 kg.

stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable if it differed systematically across the dose groups?

options.A: The 12-week duration, which was the same for every group
options.B: Daily caloric intake, which participants recorded but was not fixed
options.C: Equal sample size (n = 25) in every group
options.D: The standardized aerobic routine prescribed to every group

explanation: Correct: Caloric intake influences weight loss and was only recorded, so if it differed by dose group it could produce the apparent dose effect. Why the others are wrong: A) A duration identical across groups is a constant and cannot explain group differences. C) Equal n is not a variable affecting weight loss. D) A routine prescribed identically to all groups is held constant.
trap: Treating any listed feature as a confounder even when it is the same for all groups.

stem: The pattern of increasing weight loss with higher supplement doses best illustrates which pharmacological concept?
explanation: A dose‑response relationship occurs when greater doses produce greater physiological effects, as seen with the supplement’s incremental weight‑loss benefits.
trap: Attributing the graded weight loss to the placebo effect, although the placebo group lost only 0.7 kg.
